questions.subject: CALCULUS_I
questions.stem: For the integral of (x + 1) times the square root of x^2 + 2x + 3 with respect to x, which fact justifies choosing u = x^2 + 2x + 3?

options.text: The square root can be removed by squaring.
options.misconception: treats "The square root can be removed by squaring." as a valid result of the stated relation

options.text: Any product can be integrated by u-sub.
Derivative of x^2+2x+3 is 2x+2, proportional to x+1.
u-sub only works for exponentials.

questions.explanation: With u = x^2 + 2x + 3, differentiation gives du = (2x + 2) dx = 2(x + 1) dx, so the remaining factor (x + 1) dx is exactly half of du. That proportionality is what makes the substitution collapse the integrand. Squaring does not remove a square root, and the claim that any product works by substitution is false. Substitution is certainly not restricted to exponentials; polynomial inner functions are a standard case.
